To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the decorated processes of any PT net are a monoidal category, (2) this monoidal category is isomorphic to the monoidal category of unfoldings of the same net, (3) the decorated processes are a subcategory of $cDecOcc$ and (4) the decorated processes provide the same semantics as the token game for PT nets.
(i) decorated processes and unfolding of PT nets coincide, and (ii) decorated processes of PT nets are arrows of a symmetric closed category.

the semantics of PT-nets is given by a symmetric monoidal closed category, that is, by an algebraic model, and that this semantics is induced by the decorated occurrence nets, which in turn provide the natural unfoldings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
three main aspects.

the following three problems: (1) to provide a semantics for PT nets based on decorated occurrence nets, (2) to axiomatize the decorated processes of nets as the arrows of an algebraic model, and (3) to prove that the two approaches are equivalent.
a general theory of decorated occurrence nets and its application to the algebraic semantics of PT nets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
decorated processes, decorated occurrence nets and the category of decorated occurrence nets are all three equivalent ways of providing a semantics to PT nets.
the three semantics mentioned above coincide.
, for the class of PT nets, the three approaches to semantics can be unified and that this is achieved via a category of decorated occurrence nets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
decorated occurrence nets are the ``unified'' semantics of PT nets.
, in the context of PT nets, we have shown that the three different semantics of Petri Nets, namely the token game, the unfolding semantics and the process semantics, are equivalent.
, for PT nets, process semantics and unfolding semantics coincide, and they can be axiomatizated as a symmetric monoidal theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, by considering the history of tokens, one can give a semantics to PT nets that is both process-like and unfolding-like.
, at least for PT nets, the three different semantics of Petri net are actually equivalent.
decorated processes are a natural and powerful tool for the analysis of the behaviour of PT-nets.
